posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Ronway:

I t's not impossible to get right. Ever play the Scholar and used his Elementals? They are worded just like the other cards in question, but the Elementals rely on discard instead of damage. If you have an empty hand, can you avoid discarding? No, so the wording on the other cards are perfectly able to being read right.

 

While i appreciate the example, there is a difference in perspective between the scholar's elements and the cards which rely on damage dealt.

 

Cards that are powered by discards:

 There has never been any confusion about what "discard" means.  its in the rulebook, explicitly stated, and very easy to wrap your mind around.

 

Cards that are powered by self damage:

First of all, there has been substantial confusion about the exact meaning of "damage dealt".  Questions still come up on this forum about if damage reduction to 0 counts as damage dealt- and while they are answered swiftly, the fact that the questions arise means that confusion exists.  

Secondly, there is the question of damage immunity and damage dealt.  If you are immune to damage or redirect it, is it "dealt"?  judging by Spiff's guides, the amount of confusion on this topic (and the fact that you had to ASK this question), I would say that this was not a clear cut example!  

Thirdly, there is the damage threshold.  We're grappling with the idea that damage reduction can cause these sorts of triggers to fail, despite the willingness to "take" the damage- that global/environmental/villain effects could prevent you from dealing yourself enough damage to keep these cards around.  

Fourthly, there is the problem of going OVER the threshold- the cards specifically list an amount of damage that must be dealt…its not "at least" that much.  We could easily say that if Tachyon (for example) doesn't hit EXACTLY 2 damage on the nose for her Pushing the limits, that it would be destryed exactly as if she failed to do that much to herself.

 

We're all trying to wrap our minds around some new rules and concepts.  The last thing we need is to casually dismiss each other!

Realistically, ruling 15 will only come into play when you have chastise/embolden out AND DR to prevent the option of taking the damage. Fanatic does not get DR very often. In fact, giving her any sort of DR is usually counter productive to her deck. The situations where Fanatic is going to have DR and want to keep out one of those cards are going to be so few that you can not possibly levey the "this drastically effects her" critisism. It is wonderful hyperbole, but has no real basis.

Once you start playing the games and adapt (and it is obvious some have not yet), you will see that there is little impact to gameplay and win/loss ratio.
